title: beta-carotene attenuates calcium oxalate crystal-induced renal injury through suppression of NF-kappaB-mediated inflammation.
authors: Su, Mingqin; Guan, Yuxiang; Wei, Hongquan; Chen, Lijun; Dong, Wei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究β-胡萝卜素通过抑制NF-κB信号减轻草酸钙晶体诱导的肾损伤，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Calcium oxalate (CaOx) nephrolithiasis represents the most prevalent form of kidney stone disease and is characterized by persistent renal inflammation and tissue damage. beta-Carotene, a naturally occurring carotenoid with well-documented anti-inflammatory properties, has demonstrated beneficial effects in a variety of inflammatory conditions; however, its potential role in CaOx crystal-associated renal injury remains largely unexplored. In this study, the effects of beta-carotene on CaOx-induced renal damage were evaluated using both cellular and animal models. In human renal proximal tubular epithelial (HK-2) cells, beta-carotene effectively alleviated calcium oxalate monohydrate (COM)-induced injury, decreased kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) expression, and reduced the production of pro-inflammatory mediators, including TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, and MCP-1. Similarly, in a glyoxylate-induced nephrocalcinosis mouse model, beta-carotene attenuated CaOx crystal accumulation, improved renal histopathological alterations and functional impairment, and suppressed inflammatory responses. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were conducted. A total of 145 overlapping targets were identified, and enrichment analyses identified NF-kappaB signaling as one of the candidate pathways potentially involved in the protective effects of beta-carotene. Molecular docking analysis suggested favorable binding affinities between beta-carotene and several key targets. Experimental validation demonstrated that beta-carotene markedly inhibited NF-kappaB activation in both in vitro and in vivo settings, whereas pharmacological activation of NF-kappaB partially abolished its beneficial effects. Taken together, these findings indicate that beta-carotene ameliorates CaOx crystal-induced renal injury and inflammation, at least in part through suppression of NF-kappaB signaling, and may offer a potential basis for the development of novel preventive and therapeutic approaches for kidney stone disease.
abstract_zh: 草酸钙（CaOx）肾结石病是肾结石疾病中最常见的形式，其特征为持续性肾脏炎症和组织损伤。β-胡萝卜素是一种天然类胡萝卜素，具有充分记载的抗炎特性，已在多种炎症性疾病中显示出有益作用；然而，其在CaOx晶体相关肾损伤中的潜在作用仍 largely 未被探索。在本研究中，利用细胞和动物模型评估了β-胡萝卜素对CaOx诱导的肾损伤的影响。在人肾近端小管上皮（HK-2）细胞中，β-胡萝卜素有效缓解了草酸钙单水合物（COM）诱导的损伤，降低了肾损伤分子-1（KIM-1）的表达，并减少了促炎介质的产生，包括TNF-α、IL-1β、IL-6和MCP-1。同样，在乙醛酸盐诱导的肾钙质沉着症小鼠模型中，β-胡萝卜素减轻了CaOx晶体积累，改善了肾脏组织病理学改变和功能损伤，并抑制了炎症反应。为探究潜在机制，进行了网络药理学和分子对接分析。共鉴定出145个重叠靶点，富集分析将NF-κB信号通路确定为可能参与β-胡萝卜素保护作用的候选通路之一。分子对接分析提示β-胡萝卜素与多个关键靶点之间具有有利的结合亲和力。实验验证表明，β-胡萝卜素在体外和体内均显著抑制NF-κB激活，而NF-κB的药理学激活则部分消除了其有益效应。综合来看，这些发现表明β-胡萝卜素通过至少部分抑制NF-κB信号通路来改善CaOx晶体诱导的肾损伤和炎症，并可能为肾结石疾病的新型预防和治疗策略的开发提供潜在基础。
